name: god-rays
summary: Full-bleed hero running Paper Shaders' god rays on WebGL2: coloured volumetric shafts sweeping out of a bloom below the fold, over black, with a matched CSS ray fan as the resting state.

colors.description: Up to ten ray colours; 8-digit hex is honoured, and the upstream default leans on it to keep the violet shafts translucent. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette. Upstream default preset.

speed.description: Rate the rays sweep. 0 renders a single static frame. Forced to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion.

intensity.description: Length and reach of the rays; low keeps them near the origin, high throws them across the section.

bloom.description: Glow pooled at the ray origin, tinted by the shader's own colorBloom.

deviations.what: The noise texture is decoded before ShaderMount is constructed, so the shader starts one microtask later than a React mount would.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream's React component hands getShaderNoiseTexture() straight to ShaderMount and re-renders when it loads; a vanilla mount has no re-render, and ShaderMount throws on an image that is not complete. The image is a data: URI, so nothing is fetched.
